porbos.title: Again and Again Toward the Sky • The Row Turned in the Middle of Prayer • What the Foolish Will Say • Those Who Had Already Gone • Not in One Day • Fasting Too Came Step by Step

blocks.0: Again and Again Toward the Sky
blocks.1: Prayer is held in the mosque of Madinah. The rows stand facing north; far, very far, Bayt al-Maqdis. And behind, to the south, Makkah. There, the Ka‘bah. The house in whose shade the Prophet {{1}} grew up, the house Ibrahim (AS) built with his own hands.
blocks.2: Month after month it went on like this.
blocks.4: When the Prophet {{1}} first came to Madinah he stayed with the Ansar of his grandfathers’ clan, or, he said, of his maternal uncles’ clan. He prayed facing Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months, and he wished in his heart that his qiblah be toward the House of Allah.{{2}}
blocks.5: He wished; but no demand in words. Waiting for the command. He only looked at the sky. Once. Again. Once more. That looking too Allah was watching. The Qur’an itself speaks of that scene.
blocks.7: (O Prophet!) I see your face turning again and again toward the sky. So I will soon turn you toward a qiblah that you like. So now turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And (in future) wherever you are (while praying) keep your faces toward it. Those who were given the Book know this is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.{{1}}
blocks.8: A face rises toward the sky, falls, rises again. No complaint, no impatience. Only a silent wish. And the Lord of the heavens said, I see. This reckoning of sixteen or seventeen months is the narrator’s own; he himself said in doubt, sixteen or seventeen. By that reckoning the qiblah changed in the second year of the Hijrah, before the Battle of Badr.{{1}}
blocks.9: The Row Turned in the Middle of Prayer
blocks.10: The command came. What happened next is a picture of obedience.
blocks.12: (Toward the new qiblah) the first prayer he prayed was the ‘Asr prayer; a group of people also prayed with him. A man who had prayed with him went out and passed by the people of a mosque; they were then in ruku‘. He said, I bear witness by Allah, I have just prayed with the Messenger of Allah {{1}} facing Makkah. As they were, they turned toward the House of Allah.{{2}}
blocks.13: People bent in ruku‘. A single sentence from an unknown passer-by. And the whole row, in that very bent state, turned. No one said, let me finish the prayer first. No one said, let me go and find out for myself first.
blocks.14: The news did not reach everyone at once. Outside Madinah, at Quba, people were still praying facing the old direction. The next morning at dawn the news reached there too.
blocks.16: The people were at Quba in the Fajr prayer. Suddenly someone came and said, last night Qur’an was revealed to the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, and he has been commanded to face the Ka‘bah; so you too face the Ka‘bah. Their faces were toward Sham; they turned and faced the Ka‘bah.{{2}}
blocks.17: North to south. The whole mosque, standing in its place, turned to the opposite direction. From where the imam was, now behind the row; the row in front of the imam. Two qiblahs in one prayer. The mosque in which the first group turned in ruku‘ is well known to have later come to be known as ‘Masjid al-Qiblatayn’ (the Mosque of the Two Qiblahs). But in the narration of Sahih al-Bukhari the mosque’s name is not given.{{1}}
blocks.18: Obedience here is no longer a definition in a book. A back bent in ruku‘, which hears the command and turns.
blocks.20: Not everyone in Madinah was pleased. The direction Muslims had been praying toward all this time was the Jews’ qiblah as well. They had been pleased with it. Suddenly the direction changed.
blocks.22: The Jews and the People of the Book were pleased that he prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis. When he turned his face toward the House of Allah, they disliked it.{{1}}
blocks.23: Questions arose, taunts arose. The direction that was true until yesterday, why leave it today? The interesting thing is, the Qur’an had said this even before the question arose.
blocks.25: Soon these foolish people will say, what was it that turned them (the Muslims) away from their qiblah toward which they had been facing until now? Say, East and West all belong to Allah. He guides whom He wills to the straight path.{{1}}
blocks.26: East and West all belong to Allah. No direction has any sanctity of its own; the sanctity is of the command. Tawdih al-Qur’an has explained exactly this; no direction is worshipped by itself. The believer turns toward a direction because their Lord has told them to turn that way.{{1}}
blocks.28: Another question arose; this time from within the believers’ hearts. This was no taunt, it was pain. Those who died praying toward the old qiblah in these sixteen-seventeen months, what of their prayers?
blocks.30: (Al-Bara’ (RA)) said in this hadith of his, before the qiblah was changed, some people had died on the old qiblah, and some had been killed. We did not know what to say about them. Then Allah the Exalted revealed, Allah would never let your faith go to waste.{{1}}
blocks.31: The answer came at the end of a long verse. At the start of that verse the real purpose of the qiblah’s change is also stated.
blocks.33: (O Muslims!) In this way I have made you a middle nation, so that you may be witnesses over other people and the Messenger a witness over you. The qiblah you followed before, I appointed not for any other reason, but only because I wished to see who obeys the Messenger and who turns back on his heels; without doubt this matter was very hard, but not at all (hard) for those whom Allah had guided. And Allah would never let your faith go to waste. In truth Allah is Most Compassionate toward people, Most Merciful.{{1}}
blocks.34: Tawdih al-Qur’an says, here ‘faith’ means their prayer. The prayer prayed in obedience to the command is not lost even when the command changes.{{1}}
blocks.35: Someone died on the true path, yet one side of the path changed later. With Allah, their account is by the earlier command. A deed done in obedience to a command never goes in vain.
blocks.37: The qiblah changed in one day, in one prayer. But many other rulings did not come in one day. How many habits we have wished to leave! On the first day of the year, on the first night of Ramadan, hearing the news of a death. Then a few days. Then back to the old place. Where is the fault? In the intention? Or in trying to leave everything at once and collapsing every time?
blocks.38: ‘A’ishah (RA) said one thing to an Iraqi man. About the order in which the Qur’an was revealed.
blocks.40: What was revealed first was a surah of the Mufassal, in which there is mention of Paradise and Hell. When people turned to Islam, the rulings of halal and haram were revealed. If it had been revealed first, do not drink wine, they would have said, we will never leave wine. And if it had been revealed, do not commit adultery, they would have said, we will never leave adultery.{{1}}
blocks.41: First the heart. Then the ruling. First the fragrance of Paradise and the fear of Hell; let a reason be born within people. Then the command; then the command no longer feels like a burden. The thirteen years of Makkah were years of making the heart. Coming to Madinah, on that heart the house of rulings slowly began to rise. Even the prayer itself did not stop in one form. The prayer made obligatory in Makkah, coming to Madinah its rak‘ahs increased.
blocks.43: When Allah made prayer obligatory, He made it obligatory two rak‘ahs, two rak‘ahs, when resident and when travelling. Later the travelling prayer was kept as before, and the resident’s prayer was increased.{{1}}
blocks.44: The two rak‘ahs of travel carry to this day the memory of that first day.{{1}}
blocks.45: But even in Madinah everything did not come at once. Fasting came step by step. The prohibition of wine went step by step.
blocks.46: Fasting Too Came Step by Step
blocks.47: Even before coming to Madinah the Prophet {{1}} used to keep one fast; the fast of ‘Ashura’.
blocks.49: The day of ‘Ashura’ the Quraysh used to fast in the Jahiliyyah, and the Messenger of Allah {{1}} fasted it too. Coming to Madinah he fasted it himself and commanded fasting it. When Ramadan was made obligatory he left ‘Ashura’; then whoever wished fasted it, whoever wished left it.{{2}}
blocks.50: First one day. Then a month. The fast of Ramadan was made obligatory in the second year of the Hijrah, before Badr.{{1}}
blocks.52: O you who believe! Fasting has been prescribed for you, as it was prescribed for those before you, so that taqwa may be created among you.{{1}}
blocks.53: But in the early period even the ruling of fasting was not completely strict. One who had the ability could, if they wished, not fast and feed one poor person.
blocks.55: When it was revealed, ‘those who have the ability for it, may pay the fidyah of (fasting) by feeding a poor person’, whoever wished would not fast and give fidyah; finally the verse after it was revealed and abrogated this ruling.{{1}}
blocks.56: First a concession. People tasted fasting, a habit formed. Then the concession was lifted; now if one reaches Ramadan one must fast. Only for the sick and the traveller was there later the opportunity of qada’. And within that very verse is one sentence that tells the temper of the whole Shari‘ah.
blocks.58: Allah wishes for you what is easy, and does not wish to create difficulty for you.{{1}}
blocks.59: Another step came because of a weary Ansari.
blocks.61: The rule of the Companions of Muhammad {{1}} was, if someone was fasting and the time of iftar came, and they slept before breaking the fast, then that night and the next day until evening they would not eat. Qays ibn Sirmah al-Ansari (RA) was fasting. When iftar time came he came to his wife and said, do you have food? The wife said, no; but I will go and find some for you. He worked hard all day; sleep overcame his eyes. The wife came and seeing him said, you are deprived indeed! The next day at midday he fainted. The matter was reported to the Prophet {{2}}. Then it was revealed, ‘It has been made lawful for you on the night of fasting to go in unto your wives openly.’ They were extremely happy at this. And it was revealed, ‘Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct from the black thread.’{{3}}
blocks.62: A whole day’s labour. At iftar time no food in the house. The wife went to look; returning she found the man had fallen asleep. By the rule he could not eat any more. The next day at noon he lost consciousness. In answer to one person’s weakness a verse of ease came down from the heavens.

footnotes.1: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, Surah al-Baqarah 2:144, p. 100
footnotes.2: Date: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on the change of the qiblah in the second year of the Hijrah before the Battle of Badr’. There is disagreement among Sirah scholars about the name of the month (Rajab or Sha‘ban); it is worked out from Sahih al-Bukhari’s ‘sixteen or seventeen months’, not directly in the narration.
footnotes.5: The naming of Masjid al-Qiblatayn: a well-known report of the Sirah and the histories of Madinah, identified as the mosque of Banu Salimah; Sahih al-Bukhari 40 says only ‘people of a mosque’, no name. So the name is from the Sirah, not part of the sound hadith.
footnotes.7: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, Surah al-Baqarah 2:142, p. 97
footnotes.8: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, note 89 on Surah al-Baqarah 2:142 and note 91 on 2:143, pp. 97–99.
footnotes.9: Sahih al-Bukhari 40 (from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA); part of Zuhayr’s narration)
footnotes.10: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, Surah al-Baqarah 2:143, p. 98
footnotes.11: ‘Faith’ in the verse means prayer: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Faith, in the chapter heading of hadith 40 (‘Bab al-Salah min al-Iman’) Imam al-Bukhari brought this verse and said, ‘ya‘ni salatakum ‘inda al-bayt’; Tawdih al-Qur’an, note 92 on 2:143, p. 99.
footnotes.14: Increase of rak‘ahs in the resident’s prayer in the first year of the Hijrah: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on the increase in the prayer of the resident in the first year of the Hijrah’. The year is from the Sirah; there is no year in the hadith. The apparent discrepancy between the verse and the hadith: in Surah al-Nisa’ 4:101 it says, ‘When you travel in the land and you fear that the disbelievers will trouble you, there is no sin on you in shortening the prayer’ (Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, p. 273). From the wording ‘no sin’ it might seem that the full prayer is the original and qasr a concession. The answer through three sources: (a) In the verse of Safa and Marwah (2:158) too there is ‘la junah’, yet according to ‘A’ishah (RA) there is no leeway to leave sa‘i; when ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr understood from it that sa‘i was optional, ‘A’ishah (RA) said, ‘Nephew, you have said it very wrong’; ‘la junah’ was to remove the Ansar’s hesitation because of the Jahiliyyah idols (Sahih al-Bukhari 1643). That is, ‘la junah’ does not always signify optionality. (b) Ya‘la ibn Umayyah asked ‘Umar (RA), the verse has the condition of fear, and now people are safe; ‘Umar (RA) said, ‘I too was surprised; when I asked the Prophet {{1}} he said, this is a sadaqah that Allah has given you; accept His sadaqah’ (Sahih Muslim 686). (c) Ibn ‘Abbas (RA): Allah made prayer obligatory through your Prophet’s mouth, four for the resident, two for the traveller, one in the state of fear (Sahih Muslim 687). According to note 63 of Tawdih al-Qur’an (p. 273), qasr is obligatory in every state on an ordinary journey, whether or not there is fear of the enemy; in the verse the intention is to discuss a special kind of qasr (facing the enemy). There is disagreement among the imams on the ruling of the travelling prayer; this dars has not discussed it, only quoted the Hanafi position of Tawdih al-Qur’an.
footnotes.16: The year the fast of Ramadan was made obligatory: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on the obligation of the month of Ramadan in the second year, before the Battle of Badr’. A date from the Sirah; no sound hadith directly mentions the year.
footnotes.17: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, Surah al-Baqarah 2:183, p. 115
footnotes.19: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, Surah al-Baqarah 2:185 (part), p. 116
footnotes.20: Sahih al-Bukhari 1915 (from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA)); the translation of the inner verse portion 2:187 is from Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, pp. 117–118

porbos.title: Three Steps of Wine • The Flood of Wine in Madinah’s Lanes • Heard From Above the Seven Heavens • A New Face

blocks.1: Fasting had come as a new habit. With wine the task was the opposite; removing an old, deep habit. In the Jahiliyyah life of Arabia, wine was the soul of the gathering. Wine in poetry, wine in hospitality, wine on the night before battle. Tawdih al-Qur’an says the Arabs had been accustomed to drinking wine for hundreds of years; so Allah the Exalted adopted a gradual method to prohibit it. And even before the steps began, a hint had come in Makkah. Surah an-Nahl is a Makkan surah. Wine had not yet been made haram then. In that surah, while speaking of His own blessings, Allah said,
blocks.3: And from the fruit of the date-palm and the grapes (I give you drink), from which you make intoxicants and also good food. Surely in this too there is a sign for those who use their reason.{{1}}
blocks.4: There is no word haram in the verse. No prohibition, no punishment. Only a pair. From the same dates and grapes, two things; one wine, the other good food. And the adjective ‘good’ is placed beside the food, not beside the wine. This is that subtle hint. Tawdih al-Qur’an says, by mentioning wine in contrast to good food in this verse, a subtle hint is given that wine is not good food. After that, its evil side was brought up step by step, its use was gradually reduced, and in the end it was made haram once and for all.{{1}}
blocks.5: In Madinah ‘Umar (RA) used to make one du‘a again and again: O Allah! Give us a clear, satisfying ruling about wine.{{1}}
blocks.6: First Step: More Sin, Little Benefit
blocks.7: The first answer came in reply to a question.
blocks.9: People ask you about wine and gambling. Say, in both there is great sin, and some benefits for people too. But the sin of the two is greater than their benefit.{{1}}
blocks.10: Here haram is not said. Only the two pans of the scale are shown; on one side benefit, on the other sin. And it is said that the side of sin is the heavier.
blocks.11: Second Step: Not at Prayer Time
blocks.12: ‘Umar (RA) made du‘a again. This time a boundary line came.
blocks.14: O you who believe! Do not even go near the prayer when you are intoxicated, until you understand what you say.{{1}}
blocks.15: Five prayers a day. The gap between two prayers is small. Not being intoxicated at prayer time means staying away from wine for most of the day. In the narration of Abu Dawud: when the iqamah for prayer was called, the announcer of the Messenger of Allah {{1}} would announce, ‘Beware! Let no intoxicated person come near the prayer.’ Tawdih al-Qur’an says, in this very verse was the hint that wine is not a good thing; so at some time it might be made completely haram too.{{2}}
blocks.17: ‘Umar’s (RA) du‘a did not stop. In the end the final verse came.
blocks.19: O you who believe! Wine, gambling, altars (for idols) and divining arrows are all filth, the work of Satan. So avoid them, that you may attain success. Satan only wishes to sow enmity and hatred among you through wine and gambling, and to keep you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So say, will you (desist from those things)?{{1}}
blocks.20: ‘Will you desist?’ ‘Umar (RA) said, ‘Intahayna’; we desisted. This last step came a few years later. Far from the days of the change of qiblah. But the story is one; the story of bringing a nation out of a habit step by step.{{1}}
blocks.21: The Flood of Wine in Madinah’s Lanes
blocks.22: The scene of the day the last verse came has been told by Anas (RA). That day he was passing the cups around at a gathering.
blocks.24: I was serving wine to the people at the house of Abu Talhah (RA). At that time their wine was fadikh (wine made from unripe and ripe dates). Then the Messenger of Allah {{1}} commanded an announcer, and he announced, Listen! Wine has been made haram. Abu Talhah (RA) said to me, Go out, pour all this out. I went out and poured it out; it flowed through the lanes of Madinah.{{2}}
blocks.25: The gathering was going on. A cup in hand. Perhaps it had reached someone’s lips. An announcement. No one asked, may I take the last sip? No one said, I will give it up from tomorrow. The jars were overturned. A flood flowed in the lanes of Madinah.
blocks.26: At that very gathering some raised a question. Some Companions had been martyred before the prohibition came, and the wine was still in their bellies. What of them?{{1}}
blocks.27: The answer came in a verse.
blocks.29: There is no sin on those who believed and did good deeds for what they consumed before, if in the future they guard against sin, hold faith and remain engaged in good deeds, and (in the future from the things that are prohibited) guard themselves and remain firm in faith, and after that still adopt taqwa and ihsan. Allah loves those who adopt ihsan.{{1}}
blocks.30: On the day of the change of qiblah too exactly this question had arisen; what of those who had already gone? The same answer in two places. One who was within the command before the ruling came, Allah does not hold them to the later command.
blocks.31: Had this been done at the first step, perhaps blood, not wine, would have flowed in the lanes. After three steps one announcement was enough. When the heart is ready, the command is then not a burden; it is freedom.
blocks.32: Heard From Above the Seven Heavens
blocks.33: While the rulings were coming step by step, one day a woman came with a problem of her own. An ordinary woman. Her husband was old, and in a fit of anger had said a Jahiliyyah saying. ‘You are to me like my mother’s back.’ Tawdih al-Qur’an says, in the Jahiliyyah this saying was called zihar. By it husband and wife would become haram to each other forever; neither divorce nor a household. A suspended life.{{1}}
blocks.35: My husband Aws ibn al-Samit (RA) made zihar with me. I came to the Messenger of Allah {{1}} with a complaint. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} was talking with me about him and saying, fear Allah, he is your cousin. I did not leave from there until the Qur’an was revealed.{{3}}
blocks.36: ‘I did not leave from there.’ The Prophet {{1}} is saying, fear Allah, he is your cousin. And she goes on saying her own words. In another narration from ‘A’ishah (RA) those words of hers have come.
blocks.38: She was saying, O Messenger of Allah! He consumed my youth, I bore children for him; when my age advanced and childbearing stopped, he made zihar with me. O Allah! To You alone I complain.{{1}}
blocks.39: Youth gone, children given, now age has come. And at this age, in one sentence everything hung in the balance. When she had finished speaking to people, she raised her face toward the heavens.
blocks.40: In a corner of the house sat ‘A’ishah (RA). So close, yet the words were not reaching her ears. Later she said,
blocks.42: All praise is for Allah, whose hearing encompasses all voices. The complaining woman had come to the Prophet {{1}} and was complaining against her husband, and I was in a corner of the house; I could not hear what she was saying. Then Allah revealed, ‘Allah has heard the words of the woman who disputes with you about her husband.’{{2}}
blocks.43: The words that did not reach the corner of the next room reached above the seven heavens.
blocks.45: (O Prophet!) Allah has heard the words of the woman who disputes with you about her husband and complains to Allah. Allah hears your conversation. Surely Allah hears everything, sees everything.{{1}}
blocks.46: A woman’s domestic grief. In reply to it a whole surah, whose name even today is after her very act; al-Mujadilah, the Woman Who Disputes. This din does not regard anyone as small. And the ruling too came up the stairs of ease. First freeing a slave; if unable, fasting two months in a row; if not that either, feeding sixty poor people.
blocks.48: I said, he does not have the means. He said, then he should fast two months in a row. I said, O Messenger of Allah, he is an old man, he has no strength to fast. He said, then he should feed sixty poor people. I said, he has nothing to give in charity. Just then a basket of dates came. I said, O Messenger of Allah, I will help him with another basket. He said, you have done well. Go, feed sixty poor people with it on his behalf, and return to your cousin.{{1}}
blocks.49: In the end even the dates of the expiation came through the hand of the Prophet {{1}}. And that woman, who had come weeping, returned with an instruction: ‘Return to your cousin.’ A household did not break.
blocks.50: An event from many years later is well known. There is weakness in the chain, so it is kept as a scene. ‘Umar (RA) was then Amir al-Mu’minin. He was going along the road with people. An old woman stopped him.
blocks.52: He stopped, went to her, bent his head and listened to her, placed his hands on her shoulders; until she finished telling her need and left. A man said, Amir al-Mu’minin! For this old woman you held back the chiefs of Quraysh? He said, Woe to you! Do you know who this is? This is the woman whose complaint Allah heard from above the seven heavens. This is Khawlah bint Tha‘labah (RA). By Allah, if she had not turned away from me until night, I would not have turned away from her; only when the time of prayer came I would pray and come back again.{{1}}
blocks.53: The voice that Allah heard, the caliph did not dare to stop.
blocks.55: In Makkah Islam was weak. There, pretending outwardly to be Muslim without believing inwardly gained nothing; to become Muslim meant to be beaten. In Madinah Islam gained power in its hands. And with power came a new face; one who is one thing outside and another inside. The hypocrite.
blocks.56: Their leader became ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Why, can be understood from one incident.
blocks.58: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} mounted a donkey, with a Fadak-made cloak spread on it, and seated Usamah ibn Zayd (RA) behind him. He was going to visit Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) among the Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj; this was before the Battle of Badr. On the way he passed a gathering in which was ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul; this was before ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy’s (outward) acceptance of Islam. In the gathering were all kinds of people; Muslims, idol-worshipping polytheists, and Jews. ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA) was also in the gathering. When the dust of the mount covered the gathering, ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy covered his nose with his cloak, then said, do not raise dust on us. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} greeted them, stopped, dismounted, invited them to Allah and recited the Qur’an to them. ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy said, O man! If what you say is true, there is nothing better than it; but do not trouble us with it in our gathering. Go back to your place; tell it to whoever comes to you.{{3}}
blocks.59: A cloth over the nose. Do not raise dust. Go back to your place. And the Prophet {{1}}? He greeted them, dismounted from the mount, recited the Qur’an.
blocks.61: ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA) said, Of course, O Messenger of Allah! Come to our gatherings and recite to us; we love that. At this the Muslims, polytheists and Jews began to abuse one another, nearly coming to blows. The Prophet {{1}} kept calming them until all fell silent. Then he mounted his animal and went to Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA). He said, Sa‘d! Have you not heard what Abu Hubab, that is ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy, said? He said such and such. Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) said, O Messenger of Allah! Forgive him, pardon him. By the One who revealed the Book to you! Allah has brought the truth that He revealed to you. The people of this town had decided to crown him, to tie a royal turban on his head. When Allah, through the truth He gave you, did not let that happen, it stuck in his throat. That is why he behaved as you saw. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} forgave him.{{3}}
blocks.62: A crown was being made. The head was already chosen. Then a Prophet came, and people’s hearts turned elsewhere. The burn of a lost crown; the root of hypocrisy is right here. And the Prophet {{1}} forgave him.
blocks.63: Later, after the victory at Badr, he became Muslim outwardly, but the inner burning did not go. All his life he remained the leader of the hypocrites; that story will come in later dars. At the end of this narration of Usamah (RA) there is one sentence. The Prophet {{1}} and the Companions would then bear the harm of the polytheists and the People of the Book, and keep forgiving, until Allah gave permission.{{2}}

porbos.title: Talk of Two Faces • Three Signs of the Hypocrite • Hanzalah’s Fear • The Greatest Scholar of the Jews • Our Home Today • Final Word

blocks.1: The Qur’an has drawn a picture of the hypocrites; a very familiar picture.
blocks.3: When they meet those who believe, they say, we have believed; and when they are alone with their own devils, they say, we are with you. We were only mocking.{{1}}
blocks.4: Who are ‘their own devils’? Tawdih al-Qur’an says, those chiefs of the hypocrites who played the role of leaders and guides in their plots and conspiracies.{{1}}
blocks.5: One thing in one gathering, another thing in another gathering. The face is one; only when the house changes does the speech change.
blocks.7: How to recognise a hypocrite? One cannot see inside anyone’s heart. The Prophet {{1}} has told three signs; and they are such that must be searched for first within oneself.
blocks.9: The signs of a hypocrite are three; when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when something is entrusted to him, he betrays it.{{1}}
blocks.10: Speech, promise, trust. All three are everyday things. In the market, in the office, at home. Not everyone has a story of a lost crown like ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy. But one small lie, one broken word, one thing not returned; these can come into anyone’s life. The Companions would fear for themselves, whether this trait had crept in among them.
blocks.12: How deep this fear was can be understood from one incident.
blocks.14: Abu Bakr (RA) met me and said, Hanzalah, how are you? I said, Hanzalah has become a hypocrite! He said, Glory be to Allah! What are you saying? I said, we are with the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, he reminds us of Hell and Paradise, as if we were seeing them before our eyes. And when we leave him, we get caught up in wives, children and land work, we forget much. Abu Bakr (RA) said, By Allah, we too experience this. Then Abu Bakr (RA) and I went to the Messenger of Allah {{2}}. I said, O Messenger of Allah, Hanzalah has become a hypocrite! The Messenger of Allah {{3}} said, what is it? I told everything. The Messenger of Allah {{4}} said, By the One in whose hand is my soul! If you were always in the state you are in when with me and in remembrance, the angels would shake hands with you on your beds and on your paths. But Hanzalah, some time like this, some time like that. He said it three times.{{5}}
blocks.15: A person who is weeping, thinking themselves a hypocrite, is not a hypocrite. A hypocrite never has this fear. And the Prophet {{1}} told Hanzalah both things. The heart does not always stay at the same height; this is human nature. But this is not hypocrisy. Some time like this, some time like that. In this one sentence, what a refuge for a weary believer!
blocks.16: The Greatest Scholar of the Jews
blocks.17: The opposite picture of the hypocrite was also in Madinah. A man who said outwardly what he understood inwardly, even though it cost him his own community. ‘Abdullah ibn Salam (RA). One of the greatest scholars of the Jews. What happened in his heart on seeing the face of the Prophet {{1}} has been told in Dars 11. But he did not stop at seeing the face; he tested as well.
blocks.19: The news reached ‘Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) that the Messenger of Allah {{1}} had come to Madinah. He came to him and said, I will ask you about three things that no one knows except a prophet. What is the first sign of the Hour? What will the people of Paradise eat first? And from what does a child resemble the father, and from what the maternal uncles?{{2}}
blocks.20: The Prophet {{1}} answered all three. Hearing the answers, ‘Abdullah (RA) at once said, I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah. Then he made a request. He knew his own people.
blocks.22: O Messenger of Allah! The Jews are a people of slander. If they learn of my Islam before you ask them, they will slander me before you. The Jews came, and ‘Abdullah went inside the house. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} said, what kind of man is ‘Abdullah ibn Salam among you? They said, our greatest scholar, son of our greatest scholar; our best man, son of our best man. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} said, well, what if ‘Abdullah accepts Islam? They said, may Allah protect him from this! Then ‘Abdullah came out in front of them and said, I bear witness that there is no deity but Allah; and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. They said, our worst man, son of our worst man! And they set about slandering him.{{3}}
blocks.23: In one sentence the best. In the next the worst. In between, the man had not changed. Only which side he stood on had changed. In the very verses of the change of qiblah it is said, those who were given the Book know this is the truth. There was no lack of knowing. Between knowing and obeying, sometimes a pride stands.
blocks.24: How the Prophet {{1}} treated the Jews of Madinah is captured in one narration of ‘A’ishah (RA).
blocks.26: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah {{1}} and said, As-samu ‘alaykum (death upon you). I understood, and said, Wa ‘alaykumus-samu wal-la‘nah (and upon you death and curse). Then the Messenger of Allah {{2}} said, Stop, ‘A’ishah! Allah loves gentleness in all matters. I said, O Messenger of Allah, did you not hear what they said? The Messenger of Allah {{3}} said, I did say, wa ‘alaykum (and upon you).{{4}}
blocks.27: In the word of greeting, dropping one letter, a curse of death. And in reply one small word; wa ‘alaykum. Neither abuse nor curse. Even to speak the truth takes gentleness.
blocks.29: Every incident of this dars is still somewhere in our homes today. The first place is obedience. The people bent in ruku‘ turned at the word of a passer-by. Today when a clear ruling of the Qur’an and hadith comes before us, we first ask, what is in it for me? Does the row turn within us too?
blocks.30: The second place is the taunt about change. ‘The foolish will say’; when someone starts praying, grows a beard, takes up the hijab, we often say with a laugh, what suddenly happened? To not raise dust on the path of a person who is changing direction is the manners.
blocks.31: The third place is leaving habits. And here is a trap of wrong conclusion. Wine was not made haram in one day. It was in three steps. From there it easily comes to mind, I will also leave slowly. Here is the difference. Wine was made haram step by step because the ruling of haram was not yet complete. The day the ruling came to completion, there was no step then. One announcement, and a flood of wine in the lanes of Madinah. Today the ruling of haram stands complete. Backbiting, lying, usury, unlawful gazes; whatever Allah has made haram, today is the time to leave it. Not even a day’s delay is permitted. The phrase ‘let me reduce a little first, I will leave later’ does not apply to the haram. If it is not certain what is haram, ask a reliable scholar and find out. After knowing, no more delay.
blocks.32: Then what of one who cannot leave? There is a way for them too, but that way is not of steps; it is of repentance. Imam al-Nawawi has written three conditions of repentance. Turning away from the sin, regret for the sin, and a firm resolve not to return. The very first condition is stopping right now.{{1}}
blocks.33: If the self drags back again? Even then the door has not closed. Coming back again in shame, repenting again. The Prophet {{1}} told of Allah’s words: a servant sinned and said, O Lord! Forgive my sin. Allah said, My servant knows that they have a Lord, who both forgives sins and takes to account; I have forgiven My servant. In this way they sinned again, repented again.{{2}}
blocks.34: But this mercy cannot be made an excuse of ‘not today, tomorrow’. What is to be left today is to be left today. There is another kind of thing, which is not haram in itself but has become a habit or an addiction; too much phone, staying up late, anger. Here the lesson of the steps of wine is useful. Rather than collapsing in trying to leave everything at once, it is more useful to get the first step right. First knowing that it is harmful. Then a time limit. Then the whole. But there is one word of caution. A habit that ruins the obligatory acts, or pushes a person into the haram, is no longer merely a habit; there too there is no room for delay. And the same applies to children. That sentence of ‘A’ishah (RA); first in the heart Paradise and Hell, then halal and haram. If a list of prohibitions is handed over on the very first day, the child too may say, I will never leave. But what is haram must be taught to the child as haram too; only the manner of explaining comes step by step.
blocks.35: The fourth place is small voices. Khawlah’s (RA) words did not reach the next room, but reached Allah. In our homes, offices, mosques there are many voices we do not hear; of the domestic worker, of elderly parents, of a quiet wife, of a small child. For the voice that Allah hears, are our ears a little open to hear it too?
blocks.36: The fifth place is the signs of hypocrisy. Lying, breaking promises, betrayal of trust. Before pointing a finger at others, hold these three mirrors in front of oneself first. The sixth place is the spectacles of the group. ‘Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) became in one moment from ‘the best’ to ‘the worst’, only by changing the group. Today we too call someone good or bad by looking at their group, not at their deeds. Do we have the courage to see a person as a person?
blocks.37: The seventh place is the ups and downs of the heart. Like Hanzalah (RA), we too have one heart in the mosque, another in the market. To be disheartened by this and give up worship is a trap of Satan. Some time like this, some time like that; only taking care that the ‘like that’ does not slide into lying, breaking promises and betrayal of trust.
blocks.38: The eighth place is the reply to a bitter word. When someone says a bitter word indirectly, we return it doubled. ‘Wa ‘alaykum’; as much as was said, only that much returned. Not more than that.
blocks.40: In today’s dars several scenes came side by side. A face rising again and again toward the sky, and a row turning in the middle of ruku‘. Fasting that came step by step instead of in one day, and wine that departed in three steps. A weeping that did not reach the next room, which reached above the seven heavens. The burning of a lost crown, and a scholar who became ‘the worst’ in the eyes of his own people for the sake of the truth.
blocks.41: In all of them one single lesson; Allah knows people. He knows their weakness, knows their habits, knows their suppressed weeping. So His rulings come step by step, and His Messenger {{1}} lifts people up step by step. In the next dars we will see how, for those whose hands were tied for thirteen years, who were not allowed to hit back even when beaten, permission for self-defence came step by step.
blocks.42: So take one task from today’s dars.
blocks.44: Wine was not made haram in one day; Allah brought a nation out in three steps. But the day the ruling of haram was complete, with one announcement wine was poured out in the lanes of Madinah.
blocks.45: Today I will ask myself a question: which of my actions is haram, and which is only a bad habit? What is haram, I will leave today and repent; and for what is a bad habit, I will fix its first step; that step I will not leave from today.

footnotes.0: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 1, Surah al-Baqarah 2:14, p. 44
footnotes.1: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, note 13 on Surah al-Baqarah 2:14, p. 44.
footnotes.5: Sahih al-Bukhari 3329 (the end of the same narration)
footnotes.7: Imam al-Nawawi, Riyad al-Salihin, ‘Chapter on Repentance’: The scholars have said, there are three conditions for repentance from a sin between Allah and the servant; (1) turning away from the sin (iqla‘), (2) regret for the sin (nadam), (3) a firm resolve never to return (‘azm). If one of these is missing, the repentance is not valid. If the sin is connected to the right of a human being, then the fourth condition is returning the right to its owner or asking for forgiveness.
footnotes.8: Sahih al-Bukhari 7507 and Sahih Muslim 2758 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA); sahih): Allah accepts the servant’s repentance, however many times they return in shame. Here ‘returning’ means each time returning by leaving the sin right now, with regret, with a resolve not to go back; not taking the opportunity to delay.

Wa ‘alaykum

quiz.q: What does the change in the Jews’ remarks after ‘Abdullah ibn Salam’s (RA) Islam show?
o: Judging people by their group identity
A deficiency in their knowledge of the Torah
They did not know him at all before
They had never lied before

quiz.q: As the reason for stopping ‘A’ishah (RA) in reply to ‘as-samu ‘alaykum’, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: The Jews are our neighbours
Cursing anyone is always haram
They did not say a wrong word
Allah loves gentleness in all matters

quiz.q: Someone jabs at you with a crooked remark. What is the lesson of ‘wa ‘alaykum’?
o: Immediately return a doubled bitter word
Insult in front of everyone
Only as much as was said, not extra
Cut off the relationship for ever

quiz.q: In a political conversation a person was called ‘the best’ one day, ‘the worst’ after changing party. Which incident of the dars does it match?
o: ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy’s lost crown
‘Abdullah ibn Salam’s (RA) incident
Hanzalah’s (RA) fear of hypocrisy
Qays ibn Sirmah’s (RA) fainting

quiz.q: In an office, an employee is quiet and never complains. What should an officer learn from Khawlah’s (RA) incident?
o: To hear even the unspoken pain of silent people
One who does not complain has no problem
Speaking loudly is how one gets heard
Only written complaints are acceptable

quiz.q: Someone says, I will leave backbiting, but step by step like wine. In the light of ‘Our Home Today’, what is the reply?
o: Leaving step by step is the Sunnah, because wine also went that way
Once left, repentance is never needed again
Backbiting is a minor sin, so delay is fine
The ruling of haram is complete; stop now and repent
quiz.e: ‘Our Home Today’; Riyad al-Salihin, Chapter on Repentance.

quiz.q: According to Imam al-Nawawi’s account, what is the first condition of repentance?
o: Only regret
Turning away from the sin
Planning to leave after some days
Telling others
quiz.e: Riyad al-Salihin, Chapter on Repentance; note 1550.

quiz.q: According to the practical resolve of the dars, what is today’s task?
o: Leaving all bad habits together in one day
Leaving even haram deeds step by step, like wine
Leaving what is haram today; fixing the first step of bad habits
Correcting others’ habits
